questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was relevant for my regional studies due to the region and the language options, and I was motivated to see this regions political, societal and geographical climate.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy, it was unclear how to access some certain information, especially within the universoty itself sometimes, but it did not ruin the experience though. I felt the erasmus community info was more clear and reachable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: administation at uni, erasmus network

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, as this was informed to us through own institution and through the local one.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The transportation time it might take going from uni to campus, and tactfully plan to study near their campus to save time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student housing options were really bad. Infested with cockroaches everywhere from bed wall to fridge and mold everywhere! Administration reception was also a little suspicious and came with unclear information often.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was  comprehensible mostly, but some practical things were unclear, so I had to call several times.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: certain admin. for exchange, asking former students who were abroad the year before.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not great, almost all of them were removed, so I had to choose random ones that had to make sense for my studies back home

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Research in advance and dont be afraid to ask for help! and ask a former student who was abroad from the same course as yourself,

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I hope it makes sense when I say that the academic approach here was more "quantity over quality" in the sense that each course only had max 6 ECTS comapred to back home which offeered 15 ECTS per one course. This made it too hectic with too many exams and many practical things to look after. So you actually stress abt yourself, instead of actually learning something. Also some profs were hard to communicate with bc they didn't understand students normal questions??

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More authoritative and stricter and more traditional. Less group work, innovation and interaction, and more old-school ways of teaching. More repetition though, which actually worked better.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
KomZB050 = Media Representation, Ethics, Memory and the Holocaust (3 ECTS) 		
KomZB015 = Historical Narratives in Propaganda: Cases studies of Russia and Ukraine (3 ECTS)		
JurZM022 = International Media Law (3 ECTS)		
VestC004 = A History of Latvian Culture: the 20 Century (3 ECTS)		
VidZC001 = Environment and Sustainable Development in the Baltic Sea Region (6 ECTS)		
Valo2401 = Russian B1 (6 ECTS)		
Valo4226 = Russian B2 (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Valo2401 = Russian B1 (6 ECTS)		
Valo4226 = Russian B2 (6 ECTS) 		

Good professor with good teaching skills! 


KomZB050 = Media Representation, Ethics, Memory and the Holocaust (3 ECTS) 		
KomZB015 = Historical Narratives in Propaganda: Cases studies of Russia and Ukraine (3 ECTS)	

Interesting information and knowledge! Useful and informative, Holocaust course should almost become mandatory! .

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Many fun erasmus events arranged by the erasmus network - local, athletic and social 
Local events like folk-dancing, cultural events 
Good downtown activities like bars etc 
Museums, churches, exhibits 
Amazing theatre productions!! like ballet and opera etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Attend ESN events - great for meeting new people, getting friends and networking 
Attend local events like exhibits, local festivals and celebrations - to come closer with the culture 
Museums and important historical/memorial places  
Cinemas and theatres - be close to local and cherished art

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Attend ESN events - great for meeting new people, getting friends and networking 
Attend local events like exhibits, local festivals and celebrations - to come closer with the culture 
Museums and important historical/memorial places  
Cinemas and theatres - be close to local and cherished art   

ALSO VISIT 
national parks and nature nearby  
Go to other cities or towns nearby to not only see the capital and main cities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: not easy, local people were pretty much closed off to foreigners, and it was hard focusing on befriending locals because of courses, and the erasmus network/events

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be a part of local celebrations and be more open minded, or maybe join local social clubs at uni that are unrelated to Erasmus -   for example: film clubs/book clubs/sports clubs etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: lack of opening up, distrust of the community, too much patriotism

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: appreciation and respect of nature and folklore, mix of a double-culture identity, people were kinda closed off but always helpful nonetheless

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, do not fear the unexpected, and believe in yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: tell them to research housing options better, research courses in advance better, to make life easier - if possible, choose courses in the same campus building or in campuses near each other

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learn more about humanity and oneself, learn more about local/other cultures and what lies beneath them, learn a better discipline and be more open minded, evolving social skills

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: remaining calm under stressful situations, dealing with anxiety, trying to stay happy/positive during really grey and cold days, dealing with unfamiliar situations and not knowing what to do, finding a balance between academic and social life and also self-relaxation, getting used to a different academic system

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
